aliases: 尼泊尔君奇亚巴里茶园茶
cultivar: Mixed cultivars from India, China, Japan and Taiwan; also its own JO (Jun Chiyabari Original)
processing: Fully oxidised black tea, sold as high mountain tea. The garden makes teas across the oxidation range, with blacks, greens and whites.
harvest_season: Six harvests: early spring (March), spring (April to early May), early summer (June to mid-July), summer (to September), autumn (October to November) and winter (December).
appearance_dry: Dark twisted whole leaf, often with golden tips.
appearance_wet: Whole coppery-brown leaves and buds, as expected of a carefully made leaf tea.
taste_profile: Honey sweetness with a lingering milk-chocolate note in the Himalayan black.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for whole-leaf high mountain tea. Try it plain; it also takes shorter gongfu steeps well.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest and year, with the season named on the label: first flush lots and summer lots such as Himalayan Black 2023 are typical. Drink spring lots fresh; a fuller summer black keeps a little longer if well sealed.
description:
Jun Chiyabari is a garden near Hile in Nepal's Dhankuta district, and the name means roughly moon-lit tea garden. It is often called the country's leading producer, working between about 1,650 and 2,200 metres.

It deliberately does not call its teas orthodox. It prefers high mountain tea, and six harvests a year let it make everything from whites to full blacks from a mix of varietals.

The Himalayan black is honey-sweet with a long milk-chocolate finish. Whole leaf like this rewards water a little off the boil, and it gives more than one good steep.

The garden name and the season are usually on the label, so you can compare harvests directly. Start with a black from here, then try one of its greens to see the range.
history:
Brothers Bachan and Lochan Gyawali started the garden from scratch around 2000 or 2001; accounts give both years. Early plantings came from Darjeeling, and later ones drew on India, China, Japan and Taiwan, with the garden now starting to create its own, called JO (Jun Chiyabari Original).

It has followed organic principles from the start and gained certification in 2012. It is now moving towards natural farming in the manner of Masanobu Fukuoka.
